result.title: ACED: Reference-Anchored Aggregation of Natural-Language and Executable Evidence for Mathematical Reasoning
result.comment: 23 pages, including references and appendices. Yiyi Lu and Jiaxiang Geng contributed equally
result.summary: Natural-language self-consistency and executable programs provide complementary test-time evidence for mathematical reasoning, yet either channel may support the same semantic error. Thus we propose ACED, a reference-anchored framework that treats the self-consistency answer as the default and executable outputs as supporting evidence rather than interchangeable votes. ACED converts source-specific answer counts into smoothed supports, combines them through a weighted logarithmic pool, and overrides the reference only when a calibrated relative-evidence margin is exceeded. The same rule supports both candidate selection and admission of executable-only answers. Across five math word-problem benchmarks, ACED matches or outperforms the corresponding baselines. On GSM8K, ACED-CANDIDATE recovers 89.7% of the attainable candidate-set gain with only three damaging overrides, while ACED-ALL reaches 86.9% accuracy versus 82.6% for direct Program-of-Thought aggregation. These results show that preserving evidence provenance enables more reliable integration of natural-language and executable reasoning.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 ACED：在数学题的测试阶段把自然语言自洽答案当作默认参照，把可执行程序输出当作辅助证据而非等价投票，通过将各来源答案计数平滑为支持度、加权对数池化，并在校准后的相对证据边际被超过时才覆盖默认答案，同一规则兼顾候选选择与仅可执行答案的接纳。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「保留证据来源、异质证据通道加权汇聚、校准边际足够大才覆盖默认答案」的机制，可能可供核查 LVR 中多种 latent 假设与视觉证据的筛选、覆盖与停止决策；但该工作限于文本数学推理，不涉及视觉内部状态，迁移线索尚待验证。
